findings.explanation: Root README leads to registered container/image, data subdatasets and remodnav. The analysis consumes these root-relative trees and writes img/results_def.tex. The common-root layout is supported; the nested acquisition-source URL is separately assessed under must/002.

Following root data/raw_eyegaze reveals a nested src/lab-eyetracking module whose source is an absolute host-local path. Partial fairly distinguishes this defective reference from the public top-level data modules. The run inputs use already published eye-gaze files, so this is not evidence that the documented paper rerun needs the unavailable acquisition source.

Root dependencies are supplied through a recipe and pinned algorithm submodule. Linked labels execute python from PATH; their documented alternative invokes Condor. Those host execution dependencies are not bundled with the label module, supporting partial across the declared linked-component scope.

The frozen manifest supplies Git object IDs for source, manuscript, recipe and configuration, and Git histories for linked components. Omissions in the inspection package cannot establish uncommitted changes in the public object. The positive tracking judgment is supported independently of checkout cleanliness.

The manifest records size-bearing MD5E annex keys for image layers and raw data pointers. The raw-data README explicitly separates Git identity metadata from annex content. This establishes large-data versioning without pretending the withheld bytes were retrieved.

The root action names container/image as extra input and img/results_def.tex as outputs. In contrast the label-producing record invokes bash code/compute_all.sh, with inputs and outputs but no captured host package environment. Partial correctly credits existing action provenance while identifying its missing environment binding.

The root README is accurate and explicitly distinguishes old and updated routes. However, the assessment includes label regeneration for must/008 and other items: that linked README instructs obsolete Condor scripts while provenance executes compute_all.sh. Native verdict rule 10 caps must/007 as well as must/008 when documentation and mechanism disagree. Root-only met applies a different scope.
findings.suggested_correction: Use partial for the stated scope and credit the root instructions while naming the stale linked README. Alternatively justify and consistently apply a narrower scope across all affected criteria.

findings.explanation: The root gives a concrete results-containerized rerun and manuscript command. Following its linked label dataset leads to a README whose submit targets and Python scripts are absent from the supplied tracked inventory; the actual recorded entry point is compute_all.sh. Partial is supported for the encompassing scope.

Root input/output paths are relative. Both linked submit generators embed a particular user-home working directory and system Python 2.7. These are operational paths in the documented linked route, unlike the illustrative Windows prompt in the root README or container-internal cleanup paths.

Partial is supported by the linked host-Python route: setup.py declares libraries but compute_all.sh neither installs nor selects a complete environment. The root Docker image supplies scientific dependencies and its launcher tools are explicitly named. External installation alone is not an undocumented assumption; distinguish named host prerequisites from the incomplete label environment.
findings.suggested_correction: Ground the shortfall primarily in the linked execution environment; acknowledge the README tool/version list rather than implying those root prerequisites are wholly unspecified.

findings.explanation: The root names tested platforms and Docker compatibility. The discovered adapter assumes Docker usable by a non-root user; the linked job generator assumes a particular working directory and inherits its environment with getenv=True. Those concrete assumptions support partial. Architecture is not established from the withheld image configuration and should not be asserted as a proven defect.
findings.suggested_correction: Remove or qualify the architecture claim unless the frozen evidence establishes the image architecture. Retain the directly evidenced Docker-access and inherited-host assumptions.

findings.explanation: Root documentation names the launch tools and the recipe lists scientific/manuscript packages. The linked labels README documents obsolete commands without explaining the current Python dependency setup. This is a concrete gap in a current requirements list, supporting partial.

The extant recipe, registration, archived-image manifest and linked package metadata are committed. This item concerns version control of specifications, not their completeness or exact pinning; those are separate weaknesses and do not negate this positive.

The history contains a runnable build/save command and a later executed format-conversion command prompted by Docker compatibility changes. The README links the conversion revision and explains the supported Docker versions. This is an actual tracked maintenance instance, not merely first introduction of a specification. The upstream-duplicate flag is correct.

The root archive really is content identified; its latest tag does not make reproduction float. But met requires the property across the assessed object. The same assessment includes the label-producing computation and recognizes its missing exact environment under must/006. That route has unpinned library requirements and no recorded frozen host environment, so the root image does not establish exact replication for all in-scope computation.
findings.suggested_correction: Use partial, explicitly crediting the root archived image and identifying the linked label environment as the remaining gap. Keep the latest-tag probe override.

findings.explanation: The public recipe and archived-image locator metadata are established. A web-location log is not a successful payload retrieval, and the cohort forbids the network confirmation requested by the native procedure. Keeping live usability not-checked is defensible and appropriately avoids converting withheld payloads into a failure.

The root explains image acquisition and use clearly. For the included label-regeneration component, however, documentation points to obsolete Condor code and does not explain obtaining the environment for the recorded host-Python action. Native rule 10 explicitly includes must/017 among items capped at partial for an undisclosed documentation/mechanism conflict. A root-only positive is inconsistent with the scope used elsewhere.
findings.suggested_correction: Use partial for the stated scope, retaining the root documentation as a strength and identifying the missing current linked environment instructions.

findings.explanation: The discovery chain keeps root, input datasets, label derivatives, both algorithm revisions and the evaluation corpus under Git; annex supplements Git for large payloads. The use of two algorithm revisions does not introduce a second version-control system.

There is dated recomputation evidence and a later compatibility check, while algorithm CI runs its own package tests on a host environment. Neither establishes regular execution of the full paper instructions, and the linked README is observably stale. Partial is appropriate; no CI success was inferred from the workflow definition.

Raw inputs and event-label derivatives are separate subdatasets; algorithm code is separately linked, and study scripts, figures and image recipe have distinct locations. The actual read/write paths confirm separation beyond directory naming alone.

No restricted computational input is identified in the inspected scope, and the raw-data README expressly advertises unrestricted access. A host-local acquisition-source locator does not itself establish an access-control requirement. Empty-subject N/A is reasonable, subject to the inaccessible nested source limitation.

The historical action records successful analysis execution through the Docker adapter, whose run invocation creates a container with --rm. Native equivalent-evidence rules permit this historical clean-container evidence without a new rerun. This says nothing about fresh independent reproduction now. The external tag-based URL should be supplemented with the supplied frozen adapter hash for immutable citation.

The root registration creates a temporary HOME and the adapter starts disposable containers; its bind mount preserves declared research outputs. Linked label generation invokes the host interpreter directly with inherited PYTHONPATH. Partial therefore follows from a concrete component difference.

The recorded analysis uses the archived environment, and the later conversion first launches the old image with exit 0. That later command checks load/start compatibility, not numerical reproduction or even the converted image in a subsequent run. These intermittent checks justify partial but not regular verification of the full exact environment.

The image is an archived object within the dataset, with a recorded build/save action and content-keyed layer pointers, rather than just an external registry name. The absence of its payload in this cohort limits accessibility verification, not the demonstrated archiving design.

As for must/014, the later recorded Docker-compatibility conversion provides a concrete update after initial image creation, with commands and tracked image output. The duplicate has the same status and flag, as required; initial build alone would not have sufficed.

Explicit modules connect raw data, processed labels, algorithm implementations and evaluation corpus. This asks whether external components are linked as modules; the nested host-local source defect does not erase that mechanism.

The root instructions and declared run inputs clarify the principal composition. The linked labels documentation describes the superseded preprocessing/detection structure instead of the implemented generation route. That prevents a complete current explanation of component relationships, so partial is supported.

The stated shortfall is inability to be confident about replacement, not an identified boundary violation or update that breaks the workflow. Git pins provide independent component versioning, and the linked algorithm README documents TSV input and BIDS event output interfaces, which the assessment overlooks. Importing remodnav.tests.utils may be a stronger coupling concern, but its impact must be explained rather than substituting stale navigation documentation for this criterion.
findings.suggested_correction: Re-evaluate using interface and dependency evidence. Cite a concrete coupling that prevents independent updates if retaining partial; if the update-safety property cannot be established, use not-checked and explain the missing evidence.

findings.explanation: Gitlinks fix component revisions, the container registration selects the image, and the recorded action declares data and environment inputs together. These are concrete composition mechanisms despite documentation gaps in a linked module.

Root clone/rerun instructions and module configuration provide useful navigation. The linked README does not direct readers to its actual recorded generation script, so navigation is incomplete across the reviewed scope. Partial credits the available tooling without treating it as complete documentation.

limitations: Inspection-only review of frozen corpus remodnav-e3c6253bced7; manifest SHA256 verified as e3c6253bced7d959cd59873c3d49d166bf5793906bcdf65e49e265076d215499. No network, payload acquisition, container build or scientific execution occurred.
Binary data, figures and image payloads are absent by design. Historical recorded exits support historical execution only; present retrieval, numerical equality and payload integrity remain untested.

Followed root README/configuration and Git-module discovery paths into supplied component source and histories. The nested acquisition-source host path is unresolved; its contents and access policy could not be inspected.

Native checklist hash verification and response validation passed, independently of the substantive disagreements. All 31 native responses were checked. The response contains no aggregate score; status accounting retains 17 MUST, 9 SHOULD and 5 MAY items, including its one not-checked and one not-applicable response.

Only the assigned anonymized JSON was available for review. Its separate original probe output and narrative report were not inspected; exact probe-output counts and report-level arithmetic or labelled-goal assumptions cannot be independently confirmed.

External Docker adapter behavior was inspected from the manifest-frozen source. Its cited public version tag is weaker than a commit-pinned URL, so review citations additionally identify the frozen file by SHA256.
Model identity was not independently observable. Agreement findings are reviewer judgments, not human approval.
